BiblicalUsage: Doeg the Edomite was Saul's chief herdsman, present at Nob when David ate the showbread, and he reported it to Saul. When Saul ordered the priests killed, his own servants refused, and Doeg himself carried out the slaughter of the priests.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Doeg is the warning about what a tongue can do when it serves a jealous king. He reported what he saw, and then he did what Saul's own servants refused to do, and I take care never to let loyalty to a man overrule loyalty to God.
